name: Robert Calverley Trevelyan
bio: Robert Calverley Trevelyan (1872–1951) was an English poet and translator, a member of the Trevelyan family and a brother of the historians G. M. Trevelyan and Sir Charles Trevelyan. He published volumes of verse and verse plays, and translated Theocritus and Lucretius, among others.
Edward Marsh printed his short lyric 'Dirge' in the first Georgian Poetry volume (1911-1912); that is the poem reproduced here.

poems.title: Dirge
poems.author: Robert Calverley Trevelyan
poems.text:
Gone is he now.
One flower the less
Is left to make
For thee less lone
Earth's wilderness,
Where thou
Must still live on.

What hath been, ne'er
May be again.
Yet oft of old,
To cheat despair,
Tales false and fair
In vain
Of death were told.

O vain belief!
O'erweening dreams!
Trust not fond hope,
Nor think that bliss
Which neither seems,
Nor is,
Aught else than grief.
